subject: Aurora Council — Hosting constraints & ops check-in
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@auroracouncil.org>
Cc: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@auroracouncil.org>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Aurora Council — Hosting constraints & ops check-in

Evan / Marta — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we captured on the call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Key pain points & constraints (as discussed)
- Data residency: all inference workloads and logs must remain in EU regions; no cross-border replication.
- Regulatory driver: research group requires air-gapped processing for a subset of datasets that contain sensitive personal data (PHI-like). This implies limited or no external egress for that subset.
- Network: customer-managed outbound egress only (NAT gateway), strict IP allowlist, no direct inbound from the internet to model hosts.
- Crypto/KMS: HSM-backed key management is a hard requirement for the "air-gap" tier; procurement prefers no third-party KMS that stores keys outside customer control.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + ISO 27001 required; audit logs and 12-month retention for access logs.

Goals we heard
1) Proof of concept (2–4 week) that demonstrates in-region private hosting with HSM integration for the sensitive dataset.
2) Technical workshop next week with Aurora infra and security to validate network flow and HSM integration approach.
3) Procurement & legal review of SOW and security appendix; target decision by end of Q3.

Next steps / owners
- Laura (me): deliver network flow diagram + proposed topology (target: Fri 2027-06-20). Attachments: aurora_network_requirements_v1.pdf (network asks) + redwood_vpc_checklist.xlsx (hosting checklist).
- Rishi (cc): prep infra readiness notes and an initial scope for the POC (will join tech workshop).
- Evan / Marta: confirm available slots for a 60-min tech workshop next week and share the procurement contact (if not procurement@auroracouncil.org already).

Ask: can you confirm whether the air-gap requirement applies to all production traffic or only to the research dataset subset? That affects our proposed topology.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop. I'll follow up with the network diagram and a short agenda.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0179

Attachments: aurora_network_requirements_v1.pdf (6 pages), redwood_vpc_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Aurora Council — Hosting constraints & ops check-in

Thanks Laura — that summary is spot on.

A couple clarifications:
- The air-gap is required only for the research dataset subset today; we anticipate non-sensitive inference can be hosted in a private VPC without the air-gap constraints.
- Procurement@auroracouncil.org should be looped; please include Lina (procurement@auroracouncil.org) on procurement docs.
- Timeline: our execs want a commercial decision by the end of Q3 if the POC looks good.

Two asks for your team:
1) Can you provide a simple traffic-flow diagram that highlights egress points and where the HSM boundary would sit? A single-page sketch will do for initial review.
2) Does Redwood support on-prem HSM integrations (YubiHSM/Thales) or do you require cloud-based HSM? If on-prem HSM is supported, what's the typical integration pattern?

I'll confirm workshop availability once I check with Marta and infra — tentatively Wed/Thu next week morning CET.

Date: 2027-06-19T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurora Council — Hosting constraints & ops check-in

Evan — thanks for the clarifications and for looping procurement.

Short answers:
- Air-gap scope understood (research dataset subset only). We will prepare two architecture sketches: (A) private VPC with strict egress allowlist for general inference; (B) a hardened "air-gap tier" where compute nodes operate behind a customer-controlled NAT and keys are managed via a customer HSM with a KMS proxy.
- Yes, we support on-prem HSM integrations. Typical approach: customer exposes an HSM endpoint inside their private network (or in a connected datacenter) and we run a thin KMS proxy in the same network (or a dedicated secure tunnel) that never persists keys outside the HSM. We'll include a short integration note for YubiHSM and Thales in the diagram pack.

Deliverables & timing:
- Traffic flow diagram + HSM integration note — by EOD Fri 2027-06-20 (link to Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAuroraNetwork)
- Proposed agenda for 60-min tech workshop — within 24 hours.
- Draft SOW / security appendix for procurement — early next week.

Would Wed 2027-06-23 09:00–10:00 CET work for a workshop? If yes, I'll send a calendar invite and proposed attendee list. Please confirm procurement contact name for the SOW.

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Internal: Aurora Council POC / infra prep

Internal notes — not for customer yet. Laura, Priyom: quick engineering checklist and asks before the tech workshop.

Immediate infra asks:
- Confirm EU region availability for dedicated capacity (we typically use eu-west-1 / europe-west3); check quota with infra ops.
- Prepare a minimal topology diagram that shows: customer HSM endpoint, KMS proxy, model-hosting subnet (no public inbound), egress NAT with allowlist, and Kafka/event bridge if needed for async logs.
- Security: collect expected certs and allowed cipher suites from Aurora; confirm we can run audit logging with 12-month retention in-region.

People to loop (suggested): Soojin Lee (security lead), Diego Fernandez (solutions arch), Markus Klein (platform ops). I'll open infra ticket INT-2027-459 and attach Laura's network doc.

I'll take the action to draft the POC scope (2–4 weeks) and share a checklist by EOD Tue.

Rishi
